fetch: Perform an HTTP or HTTPS request. `input` may be a URL string, a `URL` object, or a `Request` object. `init` is an optional options object.
Request: Construct a new `Request` from `input`, which may be a URL string, a `URL`, or another `Request`.
Headers: Construct a new `Headers` collection, optionally initialized from `init`.
url: The request URL as a string.
method: The request method. Standard methods (`GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE`, `HEAD`, `OPTIONS`) are uppercased automatically.
headers: The request headers as a `Headers` object.
signal: The abort signal associated with the request, or `null`.
body: The request body as a `ReadableStream`, or `null`.
bodyUsed: Whether the body stream has already been consumed.
buffer: Consume the body and return a `Buffer`.
bytes: Consume the body and return a `Uint8Array`.
arrayBuffer: Consume the body and return an `ArrayBuffer`.
text: Consume the body and return a UTF-8 string.
json: Consume the body and return a parsed JSON value.
formData: Consume the body and return a `FormData` object. Supports `multipart/form-data` and `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` content types.
redirected: Whether the request was redirected to a different URL.
status: The HTTP status code of the response.
ok: Whether the status code is in the range 200-299.
statusText: The HTTP status message of the response.
append: Append a value to the header `name`. If the header already exists, the value is added to the existing list.
get: Get the value of the header `name` as a comma-separated string, or `null` if it does not exist.
set: Set the header `name` to `value`, replacing any existing values.
entries: Return an iterator over `[name, value]` pairs.
keys: Return an iterator over header names.
values: Return an iterator over header values.
forEach: Call `callback` for each header with the arguments `(value, name, headers)`.
